rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say a productive garden should stand on level ground; rabwa here means soft, fertile soil that swells and grows after rain.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن البستان إذا وقع في موضع مرتفع من الأرض لا تنفعه الأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He supports this soil reading with the description of earth stirring and swelling after rain.
rows.anchor: فإن المراد من ربوها ما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wābil is heavy rain with large drops and forceful impact; the garden yields its fruit or harvest to its owner or household.
rows.anchor: وصل إليها مطر كبير القطر شديد الوقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akl means the garden's fruit and yield, literally something eaten; ātat can also mean brought forth with aklahā as its sole object.
rows.anchor: أعطت صاحبها أو أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled yield is twice the usual crop because of the heavy rain.
rows.anchor: مثلي ما كانت تثمر في سائر الأوقات وذلك بسبب ما أصابها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says one year's yield equals what another garden produces in two years, so double means a like amount.
rows.anchor: حملت في سنة من الريع ما يحمل غيرها في سنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation counts four times the usual crop by taking each double as two times the thing itself.
rows.anchor: ومن فسره بأربعة أمثال ما كانت تثمر حمل الضعف على أصل معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A light drizzle suffices because the soil is excellent and the air mild; sustained drizzle can work like heavy rain.
rows.anchor: المطر الصغير القطر يكفيها لجودتها وكرم منبتها ولطافة هوائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite noun can begin a clause because it answers a conditional, a recognized license for an indefinite subject.
rows.anchor: لوقوعها في جواب الشرط وهو من جملة المسوغات للابتداء بالنكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable says sincere, strengthening expenditures are pure and never wasted, though their purity varies with intention, like a garden thriving from good soil and rain.
rows.anchor: نفقات هؤلاء الذين ينفقون بسبب ما يحملهم عليه من الابتغاء والتثبيت زاكية عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison may be distributive: divine favor and standing are the fruit, while large and small donations are heavy and light rain; both increase the result.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التشبيه من قبيل المفرق بأن يشبه زلفاهم من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees sincere work and ostentation, so the verse urges sincerity and warns against showing off.
rows.anchor: لا يخفى عليه شيء وهو ترغيب في الإخلاص مع تحذير عن الرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A discerning worshipper should seek sincerity and freedom from hidden idolatry, since release from it depends on sincere devotion.
rows.anchor: الخلاص عن الطاغوت الخفي وهو الشرك الخفي فإن الخلاص يبتنى على الإخلاص

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī warns that sowing thorns cannot yield flowers, so insincere work will not bear its hoped-for fruit.
rows.anchor: همينست ندت اكر بشنوي كه كر خاركارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pure work is done without wanting anyone to praise its doer; sincerity transforms work and multiplies its reward.
rows.anchor: وخالص الأعمال هو الذي تعملهلا تحب أن يحمدك عليه أحد

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAlī reports from the Prophet that charity speaks five benefits: it grows, is enlarged, turns an enemy into a friend, preserves what would perish, and guards its giver.
rows.anchor: إذا خرجت من يد صاحبها قبل أن تدخل في يد السائل تتكلم بخمس كلمات

rows.speaker: مكحول الشامي
rows.claim: Makḥūl says Hell asks leave to prostrate in gratitude when a believer gives charity, since the gift frees a member of Muḥammad's community from punishment.
rows.anchor: إذا تصدق المؤمن بصدقة رضي الله عنه ونادت جهنم يا رب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He assigns meanings to charity's letters: ṣād repels harm, dāl guides its giver to Paradise, and qāf signifies nearness to God.
rows.anchor: الصدقة تصد وتمنع عن صاحبها مكروه الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza denies that anyone should wish this, unlike a question denying an act already occurring; he illustrates the difference with two Arabic examples.
rows.anchor: الهمزة لإنكار الوقوع كما في قوله أأضرب أبي لا لإنكار الواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A garden can mean its dense trees; if it means the land containing them, trees must be supplied for rivers to flow beneath them.
rows.anchor: والجنة تطلق على الأشجار الملتفة المتكاثفة وهو الأنسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax of ‘all fruits’ makes it a description of provision, as in the phrase ‘each of us has an assigned station.’
rows.anchor: الظرف الأول خبر والثاني حال والثالث مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘All fruits’ means a great variety, not literally every fruit, as in the promise of every kind of fruit in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد بالثمرات العموم بل إنما هو التكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Palms and grapes are singled out as the noblest and most useful trees; other trees are included by giving these prominence.
rows.anchor: النخيل والأعناب لما كانا أكرم الشجر وأكثرها نفعا خصهما بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Old age intensifies need for the garden's benefits while making it harder to earn a living; weak young dependents cannot work or support the owner.
rows.anchor: كبر السن الذي هو مظنة شدة الحاجة إلى منافعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whirlwind is a violent revolving wind rising from the ground toward the sky like a column, carrying fire that ruins the garden.
rows.anchor: ريح عاصفة تستدير في الأرض ثم تنعكس منها ساطعة إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable depicts Judgment Day grief when good deeds are cancelled by ostentation or injury just when their doer needs them.
rows.anchor: يفعل الأفعال الحسنة ويضم إليها ما يحبطها كرياء وإيذاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its spiritual parallel is the seeker who reaches the unseen realm, then turns back to illusion and makes his effort vain.
rows.anchor: في عالم الملكوت وترقى بفكره إلى جنات الجبروت ثم نكص على عقبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Thus’ points back to clear explanations of striving and spending for God and the stories of Abraham and Ezra; the signs establish monotheism and the truth of religion.
rows.anchor: البيان الواضح الذي بين فيما مر من الجهاد والإنفاق في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs call readers to reflect, learn from their lessons, and act accordingly.
rows.anchor: تتفكروا فيها وتعتبروا بما فيها من العبر

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Qushayrī contrasts sincere and hypocritical spending: some receive replacement and honor, while others waste, lose their wealth, and have their deeds nullified.
rows.anchor: ذكرها الله على جهة ضرب المثل للمخلص والمنافق والمنفق في سبيل الله والمنفق في الباطل

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Qushayrī likens faithful deeds to a flourishing crop and failed deeds to a ruined bargain that leaves an old person without income.
rows.anchor: أنبت زرعا زكا أصله ونما فضله وعلا فرعه وكثر نفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Works need sincerity because their fruits depend on their root.
rows.anchor: فلا بد من إخلاص الأعمال فإن الثمرات تبتنى على الأصل

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muʿādh reports that, when he was sent to Yemen, the Prophet advised him to make his religion sincere, making a little work sufficient.
rows.anchor: حين بعث إلى اليمن يا رسول الله أوصني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treat ostentation by removing its roots and establishing its opposite; its main causes are love of this world and preferring immediate pleasure to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قطع عروقه واستئصال أصوله وذلك بإزالة أسبابه وتحصيل ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before each worship act, inspect the heart, remove thoughts of ostentation, resolve on sincerity, and keep resisting them.
rows.anchor: فعليك في أول كل عبادة أن تفتش قلبك وتخرج منه خواطر الرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ostentation enters in three stages: expecting people to notice, wanting their praise and status, then accepting and settling on that desire; reject each.
rows.anchor: العلم باطلاع الخلق أو رجاؤه ثم الرغبة في حمدهم وحصول المنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭayyib can mean lawful or good-quality earnings; the command excludes unlawful giving while ‘spend what you love’ supports the quality reading.
rows.anchor: من حلال ما كسبتم أو جياده

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's Kashshāf glosses ṭayyib as the best of one's earnings.
rows.anchor: الطيبات بالجياد حيث قال من طيبات ما كسبتم

rows.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
rows.claim: Some scholars prefer ‘good-quality’ over ‘lawful’: the command already excludes unlawful gifts, and khabīth below means inferior.
rows.anchor: فسر الطيب بالجيد دون الحلال لأن الحل استفيد من الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's produce includes grains, fruits, and minerals; taya mmu means to aim for, and khabīth means inferior or base.
rows.anchor: من الحبوب والثمار والمعادن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭayyib and khabīth each have three senses: lawful and forbidden, pure and impure, or pleasing and repugnant to natural taste.
rows.anchor: الطيب الحلال والخبيث الحرام والطيب الطاهر والخبيث النجس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposed phrase restricts the prohibited practice: do not target inferior goods as the sole charity; the wording censures that habit.
rows.anchor: والتخصيص لتوبيخهم بما كانوا يتعاطونه من إنفاق الخبيث خاصة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says people used to give away rotten and inferior dates, which they were forbidden to do.
rows.anchor: أنهم كانوا يتصدقون بحشف التمر وشراره فنهوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People would not accept inferior goods in a transaction except reluctantly, such as taking poor property for a sound debt for fear of losing the claim or from need.
rows.anchor: لو كان لكم على رجل حق فجاء برديء ماله بدل حقكم الطيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom ‘overlook’ asks a seller not to press every detail, as if he were looking away; God is self-sufficient and commands giving for donors' benefit.
rows.anchor: من قولك أغمض فلان عن بعض حقه إذا غض بصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A promise is information about what the speaker will bring about later, and the word can describe a bad outcome as well as a good one.
rows.anchor: الوعد هو الإخبار بما سيكون من جهة المخبر مترتبا على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an calls Hell a promise to disbelievers, showing that the word applies to harm too.
rows.anchor: النار وعدها الله الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan frightens people with poverty and tells them to keep their wealth lest charity make them poor.
rows.anchor: فإنك إذا تصدقت به افتقرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāḥshāʾ here is stinginess and withholding charity; Arabs call a miser fāḥish.
rows.anchor: يغريكم على البخل ومنع الصدقات إغراء الآمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises forgiveness and replacement greater than what was spent in this world, as well as reward in the next, refuting Satan.
rows.anchor: خلفا مما أنفقتم زائدا عليه في الدنيا وثوابا في العقبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has ample power and bounty to fulfill His promise and knows each gift, so He does not waste its reward.
rows.anchor: فيحقق ما وعدكم به من المغفرة وإخلاف ما تنفقونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children are singled out because people defend themselves with wealth as ransom or by relying on children; if unbelievers gain nothing from either in the afterlife, other things help them even less.
rows.anchor: لأن الإنسان يدفع عن نفسه تارة بفداء المال وتارة بالاستعانة بالأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers are companions of the Fire, remaining with it forever.
rows.anchor: أي مصاحبوها على الدوام وملازموها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers the thought that unbelievers might benefit from charitable spending: they do not benefit even when they intend God's pleasure.
rows.anchor: بين أنهم لا ينتفعون بتلك الإنفاقات وإن كانوا قد قصدوا بها وجه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers may spend for worldly benefit, afterlife reward, public praise, or hostility toward Muslims; Abū Sufyān and companions spent heavily at Badr and Uḥud.
rows.anchor: طلبا لحسن الذكر بين الناس وعداوة لأهل الإسلام كما أنفق أبو سفيان وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣirr is a devastating cold, originally a verbal noun but commonly used for a cold wind; it strikes the harvest of people who wronged themselves through unbelief and sin.
rows.anchor: برد شديد مهلك فإنه في الأصل مصدر وإن شاع إطلاقه على الريح البارد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind completely destroys the harvest, just as their spending vanishes without benefit; God does not wrong them, since they spent wrongly.
rows.anchor: تشبيه ما أنفقوا في ضياعه وذهابه بالكلية من غير أن يعود إليهم نفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if unbelievers built hostels and bridges or helped the weak, orphans, and widows hoping for reward, unbelief nullifies the good and leaves grief like a burned crop.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك المنفق يرجو من ذلك الإنفاق خيرا كثيرا فإذا قدم الآخرة رأى كفره مبطلا

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: A saying attributed to one of the great elders says a trial reveals whether a person is honored or disgraced.
rows.anchor: وعند الامتحان يكرم الرجل أو يهان عصمنا الله وإياكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammatical object of ‘do not think’ is omitted but supplied by ‘their stinginess’: stinginess is not better than spending and is worse because it brings punishment.
rows.anchor: المفعول الأول محذوف لدلالة يبخلون عليه أي ولا يحسبن البخلاء بخلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collar is a representative metaphor for the unavoidable burden and sin of stinginess; another view takes it literally as a snake or fiery collar, with a hadith to follow.
rows.anchor: سيلزمون وبال ما بخلوا به الزام الطوق إذ لا طوق ثمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth belong to God alone; people should not withhold wealth from its owner, and what they keep remains behind at death with regret.
rows.anchor: وحده لا لأحد غيره استقلالا واشتراكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows both withholding and giving and recompenses them.
rows.anchor: من المنع والإعطاء {خبير} فيجازيكم على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bukh means refusing a duty, not declining optional charity; duties include supporting oneself and dependents, famine relief, and needed military aid.
rows.anchor: البخل عبارة عن امتناع أداء الواجب والامتناع عن التطوع لا يكون بخلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritually, stinginess turns God's gift into misery, while generosity makes it a blessing leading to happiness and Paradise.
rows.anchor: بإكسير البخل يجعلون خيرية ما آتاهم الله من فضله شرا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love of wealth is like a collar around the heart and breeds miserliness, greed, envy, rancor, hostility, pride, anger, and other vices.
rows.anchor: تحيط بالقلب ومنها تنشأ معظم الصفات الذميمة مثل البخل والحرص والحسد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet calls love of this world the root of every sin; withholding zakat wraps the luminous spirit in low, dark traits and their veils.
rows.anchor: حب الدنيا رأس كل خطيئة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says a person who fails to pay zakat will wear a bald serpent with two dark marks as a collar; it grips his jaws, identifies itself as his wealth, and the Prophet recites this verse.
rows.anchor: من آتاه الله مالا فلم يؤد زكاته مثل له يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A second report says withheld zakat becomes a snake around the neck that bites from head to foot and pecks the head, saying it is the owner's wealth.
rows.anchor: يجعل ما بخل به من الزكاة حية يطوقها في عنقه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Those who withhold the due on livestock will be trampled and gored by their animals repeatedly until judgment is completed.
rows.anchor: ما من رجل يكون له إبل أو بقر أو غنم لا يؤدي حقها

rows.speaker: أبو حامد
rows.claim: Abū Ḥāmid describes the withheld due as an enormous camel, bull, sheep, grain sacks, or heavy snake carried on the owner's shoulders while angels identify it as what he hoarded.
rows.anchor: مانع زكاة الإبل يحمل بعيرا على كاهله له رغاء وثقل

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says zakat protects wealth, charity treats illness, and supplication meets calamities; he also says prayer is invalid without zakat.
rows.anchor: حصنوا أموالكم بالزكاة وداووا مرضاكم بالصدقة واستقبلوا البلايا بالدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses admires a man's focused prayer, but God says even vast prayer, emancipation, funerals, pilgrimage, and campaigns are useless until zakat is paid.
rows.anchor: مر برجل وهو يصلي مع حضور وخشوع

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet calls wealth without annual zakat and a body never tested within forty nights accursed; trials include falls, illness, scratches, and eye twitching.
rows.anchor: ملعون مال لا يزكي كل عام وملعون بدن لا يبتلي في كل أربعين ليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports show the burden of persistent refusal to pay zakat freely and with a willing heart, even after wealth and circumstances favor the owner.
rows.anchor: وقفت على وزر من وقف على الإصرار ولم يؤد زكاة ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccans asked the Prophet for a sign proving his claim because he called them to worship God alone; the verse answered with signs in creation.
rows.anchor: أهل مكة سألوا رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام أن يأتيهم بآية لصحة دعواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs lie in the great creation of heaven and earth, including sun, moon, stars, mountains, seas, trees, wild animals, and birds.
rows.anchor: من الشمس والقمر والنجوم وما خلق الله في الأرض من الجبال والبحار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation may mean night departing and day arriving, or their changing colors and lengths as each grows while the other shrinks with the sun's seasonal distance.
rows.anchor: يعني ذهاب الليل ومجيء النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lubb is the pure core of intellect: the mind first has ordinary reason and reaches its perfected inner core at the end of development.
rows.anchor: واللب خالص العقل فإن العقل له ظاهر وله لب ففي أول الأمر يكون عقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of understanding remember God in all conditions, standing, sitting, and lying down, the postures in which people generally find themselves.
rows.anchor: أي يذكرونه دائما على الحالات كلها قائمين وقاعدين ومضطجعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verse calls the present world a prison for souls and urges travel toward the soul's open country.
rows.anchor: اين جهان خود حبس جانهاي شماست هين رويد آن سوكه صحراي شماست

rows.speaker: العطار
rows.claim: ʿAṭṭār urges removing the veil from the sun, crossing bodily Mount Qāf toward the spiritual kingdom, and refusing pride in this false realm where wealth and honor pass.
rows.anchor: نقاب ازروي ون خورشيد بردار اكر هستي زروي خود خبر دار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance is unavailable to those who continue sinning until death throes and see the angel of death; that is compulsion rather than choice.
rows.anchor: وقع في سكرات الموت وشاهد ملك الموت سوى علاماته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial also applies to those who die unbelievers and repent only near death or on seeing punishment; both groups face prepared, painful punishment.
rows.anchor: مصرون على كفرهم إذا تابوا عند قرب الموت أو عند معاينة العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Equating a deathbed procrastinator with an unbeliever stresses that neither has valid repentance then, urging sinners to seek forgiveness promptly.
rows.anchor: سوى بين من سوف التوبة وأخرها إلى حضور الموت من الفسقة

rows.speaker: جلال الدين رومي
rows.claim: Rūmī says to repent for earlier sins and trust that God accepts; divine care makes a person hasten to repent when even a small reminder moves him.
rows.anchor: كرسيه كردي تونامة عمر خويش

rows.speaker: السري السقطي
rows.claim: Al-Sarī al-Saqaṭī says he found Bahlūl in a cemetery; Bahlūl replied that the dead do not harm him or gossip when he is away.
rows.anchor: خرجت يوما إلى المقابر فإذا ببهلول فقلت له أي شيء تصنع هنا

rows.speaker: بهلول
rows.claim: Bahlūl left when hungry and recited that hunger is a pious act and prolonged hunger will eventually be followed by satisfaction.
rows.anchor: أجالس قوما لا يؤذونني وإن غبت لا يغتابونني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A king's parable shows God adorning chosen lovers with righteous deeds and pure states: they need not display themselves to ordinary people, since God knows and their rank will be seen at the great gathering.
rows.anchor: فهذا مثل من وفقهم الله تعالى للأعمال الصالحة والأحوال الزكية ولا حاجة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet contrasts the noble servants of God with the speaker's group as wretched slaves.
rows.anchor: أولئك خدام كرام وسادة ونحن عبيد السوء بئس عبيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor wool-clad believers such as Ṣuhayb, ʿAmmār, Khabbāb, Bilāl, and Salmān so they could retain his company and status before Arab visitors.
rows.anchor: حين رأوا في مجلسه الشريف فقراء المؤمنين

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet refused to expel believers, though he considered separating them to attract Quraysh; revelation taught that religion does not privilege the rich over the poor.
rows.anchor: ما أنا بطارد المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expulsion means removal; morning and evening remembrance signifies continuity, and whoever remembers continually remains with God.
rows.anchor: الطرد الإبعاد وبالفارسية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says, ‘I am the companion of whoever remembers Me.’
rows.anchor: أنا جليس من ذكرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor worshippers seek God's face and pleasure alone, not worldly aims.
rows.anchor: بذكرهم وعبادتهم {وجهه} تعالى ورضاه لا شيئا من أغراض الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Seeking His face’ is circumstantial to ‘they call’; it stresses that sincerity is the essential point of supplication.
rows.anchor: يدعونه تعالى مخلصين له وقيد الدعاء بالإخلاص تنبيها على أنه ملاك الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet says worship is good when intention is sincere; without that, it is like a kernel-less grain.
rows.anchor: عبادت بإخلاص نيت نكوست وكرنه ه آيد زبى مغزوست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's face is among the strongest grounds for honor and is incompatible with expelling poor worshippers.
rows.anchor: من أقوى موجبات الإكرام المنافي للأبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh not only disparaged poor believers' status but alleged their faith was false and that they gathered for food and clothing; God rejects this as grounds for expulsion.
rows.anchor: في طعن فقراء المسلمين على وصفهم بكونهم موالي ومساكين بل طعنوا في إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must judge by their outward mark of piety; any hidden defect in faith harms only them, not him, so he should welcome and nurture them.
rows.anchor: ليس عليك إلا اعتبار ظاهر حالهم وهو اتسامهم بسمة المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated denial of responsibility emphasizes that their reckoning is no concern of the Prophet, just as his is no concern of theirs.
rows.anchor: مع أن الجواب قد تم بما قبله للمبالغة في بيان انتفاء كون حسابهم عليه

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abū al-Suʿūd says the repeated phrase emphasizes the point by pairing it with the uncontroversial reverse; ‘then you expel them’ answers the prohibition's logic.
rows.anchor: قال المولى أبو السعود : وذكر قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Thus We tested them’ points to God's giving poor believers precedence in religion by granting faith despite their poor worldly condition, while the rich had worldly precedence.
rows.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى مصدر ما بعده من الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed kāf intensifies the demonstrative: God tried them with a complete and remarkable trial.
rows.anchor: والكاف مقحمة لتأكيد ما أفاده اسم الإشارة من الفخامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Some by others’ means people are tested through one another, especially as poor believers are raised above worldly superiors in religion.
rows.anchor: بعض الناس ببعضهم لافتون غيره حيث قدمنا الآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in ‘so that they say’ marks the outcome: worldly elites belittle the poor because of visible disparity while ignoring the real criterion of merit.
rows.anchor: اللام للعاقبة أي ليكون عاقبة أمرهم أن يقول البعض الأولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighing on that Day distinguishes deeds that are weighty or light, good or bad.
rows.anchor: راجحها وخفيفها وجيدها ورديها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavy scales means the person's good deeds; mawāzīn may mean weighed things or balances, with the plural reflecting distinct objects or weighings.
rows.anchor: حسناته التي توزن فهو جمع موزون ويجوز أن يكون جمع ميزان

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmī taʾwīl says every servant has several just balances suited to bodily attributes, spiritual qualities, secret states, and hidden ethics.
rows.anchor: بالجمع لأن كل عبد ينصب له موازين بالقسط تناسب حالاته

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The hidden spiritual faculty receives divine moral qualities; the Prophet says good character is the heaviest thing on the scale because people are commanded to emulate God's qualities.
rows.anchor: ما وضع في الميزان أثقل من حسن الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ‘those’ follows the plural sense of ‘whoever,’ and the separate pronoun ‘they’ restricts the predicate to the successful.
rows.anchor: ضمير فصل يفيد اختصاص المسند بالمسند إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful are those who win salvation and reward.
rows.anchor: الفائزون بالنجاة والثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Light scales reflect sins; those who lose themselves have damaged their sound original nature and earned punishment through their deeds.
rows.anchor: بتضييع الفطرة السليمة التي فطرت عليها واقتراف ما عرضها للعذاب

rows.speaker: الحدادي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥaddādī defines loss as losing one's capital; a person's capital is the self, so destroying it through bad deeds is self-loss.
rows.anchor: الخسران إذهاب رأس المال ورأس مال الإنسان نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wronging God's signs means placing denial where belief should be; grammatically, ‘what’ is a verbal noun and ‘by Our signs’ modifies ‘wronging’ with denial implied.
rows.anchor: وضعوا التكذيب بها موضع التصديق

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmī taʾwīl says the scale weighs people of truth and good deeds, not falsehood and its adherents; it cites the promise that no weight will be set for them.
rows.anchor: الوزن عند الله يوم القيامة لأهل الحق وأرباب الصدق وأعمال البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes a huge, tall, gluttonous man who weighs less than a mosquito's wing, supporting the view that people themselves may be weighed.
rows.anchor: يؤتى يوم القيامة بالرجل العظيم الطويل الأكول الشروب فيوزن فلا يزن جناح بعوضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars say people are weighed, but the majority say deed records are weighed on a two-pan scale before witnesses to demonstrate justice and remove excuses.
rows.anchor: ولكن الجمهور على أن صحائف الأعمال هي التي توزن بميزان له لسان وكفتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report has ninety-nine long scrolls weighed against a small card with the two testimonies; the scrolls fly up while the card weighs more.
rows.anchor: يؤتى به إلى الميزان فينشر له تسعة وتسعون سجلا مدى البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A card was a small tag sewn into a garment to record its price.
rows.anchor: والبطاقة رقعة صغيرة وهي ما يجعل في طي الثوب يكتب فيها ثمنه

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: Dāwūd asks to see the Judgment scale and faints at its vast size; God says one date of charity can fill it if He is pleased with the servant.
rows.anchor: أن داود عليه السلام سأل ربه أن يريه الميزان الذي ينصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each destroyed nation has a fixed term for annihilation; the singular pronoun means each nation has its own appointed time.
rows.anchor: حد معين من الزمان مضروب لمهلكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When its hour arrives, they cannot delay at all; ‘hour’ figures a tiny span and the emphatic form signals helplessness despite wanting delay.
rows.anchor: شيئا قليلا من الزمان فإنها مثل في غاية القلة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also cannot arrive before the appointed time.
rows.anchor: لا يتقدمون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet says that when a person's appointed term comes, it cannot be delayed or advanced.
rows.anchor: اجل ون فردا آيدت يش وس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A king abandons asceticism for worldly rule and builds a palace; a voice reminds him death is fixed, so he gives up entertainments, repents, and dies repeating ‘death.’
rows.anchor: كان متنسكا ثم رجع ومال إلى الدنيا ورياسة الملك

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī's Persian verses warn that worldly houses become ruins and gardens thorn growth.
rows.anchor: خانه از اي بست ويرانست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, each community of travelers to God, Paradise, or Hell has a fixed period and respite assigned by God.
rows.anchor: لك قوم من السائرين إلى الله وإلى الجنة وإلى النار مدة معلومة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmī taʾwīl treats the fixed term as reassurance to God's friends and a threat disciplining His enemies.
rows.anchor: هذا وعد للأولياء استمالة لقلوبهم ووعيد للأعداء سياسة لنفوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Children of Adam’ addresses everyone; immā is formed from in and emphatic mā, and the conditional frames the arrival of messengers from humankind.
rows.anchor: أصله إن ما ضمت كلمة ما إلى إن الشرطية تأكيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers are human and are described as reciting God's signs, meaning they explain His rulings and laws.
rows.anchor: من جنسكم فهو صفة لرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although their coming is certain in God's knowledge, conditional ‘if’ shows sending messengers is neither rationally nor legally obligatory upon God, though wisdom calls for it.
rows.anchor: لكون الإتيان محقق الوقوع في علم الله تعالى لكنه سيق المعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Then He turned to them’ repeats the assurance to stress that God pardoned their lapse in view of the hardship they endured.
rows.anchor: تجاوز عن ذنبهم الذي فرط منهم وهو تكرير للتأكيد

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Ḥāfiẓ's couplet says no one reaches ease on the path of seeking without enduring hardship.
rows.anchor: مكن زغصه شكايت كه در طريق طلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is compassionate and merciful; the attributes explain pardon, may mean removing harm and giving benefit, and include sending His beloved Messenger and miracles.
rows.anchor: فإن صفة الرأفة والرحمة من دواعي التوبة والعفو

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: During Tabūk's water shortage, Abū Bakr asks the Prophet to pray; rain falls over the army alone until people are replenished and store water.
rows.anchor: شكوا للنبي عليه السلام عسرة الماء في غزوة تبوك فقال أبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In another Tabūk report, the Prophet's fingers make water well from a nearly empty vessel and serve the thirsty army, including 12,000 horses, 15,000 camels, and 30,000 or 70,000 people.
rows.anchor: فنبع الماء بين أصابعه العشر وأقبل الناس واستقوا

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: When famine threatens, ʿUmar advises against slaughtering transport animals and asks the Prophet to gather leftover provisions and pray for blessing.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر رضي الله عنه يا رسول الله إن فعلت فني الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet blesses a small pile of food; it fills every container, feeds everyone, and leaves some over. He testifies that a non-doubting believer in the two testimonies is protected from Hell.
rows.anchor: فأخذوا حتى ما تركوا في العسكر وعاء إلا ملؤوه وأكلوا حتى شبعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The three left behind’ are those whose case was deferred without a ruling until revelation: Kaʿb ibn Mālik, Murāra ibn al-Rabīʿ, and Hilāl ibn Umayya.
rows.anchor: وتاب الله على الثلاثة الذين أخر أمرهم ولم يقطع في شأنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth became narrow when people avoided speaking or even greeting them; they feared dying without the Prophet or believers praying over them.
rows.anchor: لأعراض الناس حتى عن المكالمة معهم ولو بالسلام ورده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their souls were so filled with loneliness that no room remained for comfort or joy; saying these were constricted ‘upon them’ stresses their utter distress.
rows.anchor: ما يسع شيئا من الراحة والأنس والسرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They knew there was no refuge from God's anger except turning to Him for forgiveness; ‘they thought’ means ‘they knew,’ since this is praise and praise requires knowledge.
rows.anchor: علموا وأيقنوا أن لا ملاذ ولا خلاص من سخطه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, an omitted pronoun of ‘the matter’ is the subject of softened anna; the clause fills both objects of ‘they thought,’ with exception from an omitted general term.
rows.anchor: اسمها ضمير شأن مقدر ولا مع ما في حيزها خبران

rows.speaker: بعض المتقدمين
rows.claim: An early saying advises frequent gratitude when blessings accumulate and frequent seeking forgiveness when worries multiply.
rows.anchor: من تظاهرت عليه النعم فليكثر الحمدومن كثرت همومه فليكثر الاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One immersed in divine unity sees only God in existence and seeks refuge only in Him; visible forms and places are merely causes.
rows.anchor: من توغل في بحر التوحيد بحيث لا يرى في الوجود إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rūmī's Mathnawī compares a visible form to a shadow and urges seeking the reflected person, turning from secondary causes to the ultimate Causer.
rows.anchor: كره سايه عكس شخص است اي سر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Then He turned to them’ means He enabled them to repent; ‘so they might repent’ means they returned from sin.
rows.anchor: وفقهم للتوبة {ليتوبوا} ليرجعوا عن المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes God's enabling, the person's repentance, and God's acceptance; enabling precedes acceptance by two ranks, so thumma signals rank rather than time.
rows.anchor: التوفيق للتوبة ، وهو ما دل عليه قوله ثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘He turned to them’ means He announced acceptance and ‘so they might repent’ means they became counted among the repentant; thumma then keeps its ordinary temporal sense.
rows.anchor: أي أنزل قبول توبتهم ليتوبوا أي ليصيروا من جملة التوابين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is repeatedly accepting and merciful, accepting a repentant person even after a hundred returns while favoring people who deserve punishment.
rows.anchor: البالغ في قبول التوبة لمن تاب وإن عاد في اليوم مائة مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet says repentance needs hope of acceptance and a broken or uncertain vow does not complete sincere repentance.
rows.anchor: هم توبه شكسته است وهم يمان سست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some believers who had lagged behind regretted it and caught up with the Prophet.
rows.anchor: روي أن ناسا من المؤمنين تخلفوا عن رسول الله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan recounts three cases: one leaves a valuable orchard that held him back, another his family, and a third his love of life; each crosses hardship to rejoin the Prophet.
rows.anchor: بلغني أنه كان لأحدهم حائط كان خيرا من مائة ألف درهم

rows.speaker: أبو ذر الغفاري
rows.claim: Abū Dharr's camel delayed him, so he carried his belongings on his back and followed the Prophet on foot.
rows.anchor: أبعيره أبطأه فحمل متاعه على ظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathered pious are brought before the Merciful as honored guests; people recognize each other as in worldly life, as if death were only a brief separation.
rows.anchor: يعرف بعضهم بعضا كما كانوا يعرفون في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recognition later stops when they see punishment, and they disown one another; the verse declares and marvels at the loss of those denying meeting God.
rows.anchor: ثم ينقطع التعارف إذا عاينوا العذاب ويتبرأ بعضهم من بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were cheated in their trade, exchanging faith for unbelief and truth for denial, with no benefit left once time had passed.
rows.anchor: غبن المكذبون بالحساب والجزاء وما كانوا مهتدين في تجارتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian saying has a teacher tell a child that they did no work and the day has passed, warning against wasting life.
rows.anchor: كه كارى نكرديم وشد روز كار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Prophet sees some promised punishment in life, as at Badr, that is the hoped-for outcome; if he dies first, the people return to God and are punished in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: بأن نظهر لك بعض الذي نعدهم من العذاب ونعجله في حياتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘If We show you’ combines in with emphatic mā and omits an obvious answer; another passage supports the alternatives because return to God follows death and cannot answer both conditions.
rows.anchor: رجوعهم رجوعا اضطراريا فنريكه في الآخرة وإنا منهم منتقمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘God is witness over what they do’ means He will recompense their evil deeds; witness stands for its consequence, and delayed ordering suits their return.
rows.anchor: ذكر الشهادة وأراد نتيجتها ومقتضاها ولذلك رتبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse connects to an implied preceding clause: God destroys past peoples, then saves messengers and believers as if narrating those past events in the present.
rows.anchor: عطف على محذوف دل عليه قوله : مثل أيام الذين خلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Just so’ describes deliverance; ‘truly upon Us’ interrupts the verb and object, with an understood verb meaning the promise is truly established.
rows.anchor: اعتراض بين الفعل ومعموله ونصبه بفعله المقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's established practice is to save believers from every hardship and punishment, as He saved earlier messengers and followers and fulfilled His promise; this continues while the law and its practice remain.
rows.anchor: كما أنجى الرسل المتقدمين ومن آمن بهم وأنجز ما وعد لهم

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī's couplet says a beloved who loves you will not leave you in an enemy's hands.
rows.anchor: محالست ون دوست دارد ترا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet calls death a believer's gift: the righteous rest from worldly toil in barzakh, while the wicked relieve others of harm and enter spiritual punishment.
rows.anchor: فأن الموت تحفة المؤمن ، ألا ترى إلى قوله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best worship is waiting for relief because it brings ease of heart and patience's reward; trusting that God alone removes affliction reduces pain and panic.
rows.anchor: أفضل العبادة انتظار الفرج وذلك لأن فيه استراحة القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ignorant sufferer may forget divine decree and gentleness, think relief impossible, implicitly attribute impotence to God, and remain distressed.
rows.anchor: بخلاف حال الجاهل الذي لا يخطر بباله أن ما يجري عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling earlier prophets and believers who endured harm and remained steadfast, the Prophet too should persist in monotheism and its call until God's command arrives.
rows.anchor: أحوال القرون الأولى وأن إخوانك الأنبياء ومؤمنيهم تحملوا من قومهم الأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Those who repented with you’ coordinates with the implicit subject of ‘be steadfast’; they are believers who turned from unbelief and share faith, not a claim that prophets repented from unbelief.
rows.anchor: معطوف على المستكن في فاستقم من غير تأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets are unanimously protected from unbelief and deliberate major sins before and after revelation; shared repentance can mean turning together without sharing the same past sin.
rows.anchor: معصومون عن الكفر وكذا عن تعمد الكبائر قبل الوحي وبعده بالإجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests repentance here means leaving one's former state, whether it involved actual unbelief or not, as with the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لعل التوبة في مثل هذا المقام هي الرجوع عن الحالة الأولى ومفارقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet testified that ʿAlī never disbelieved in God even for an instant; inviting him to reject al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā does not prove he had been an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: شهد بأن عليا رضي الله عنه لم يكفر بالله قط طرفة عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not transgress the set limits through excess or deficiency, since both extremes are blameworthy; ‘transgression’ emphasizes the warning or generalizes from most believers.
rows.anchor: أي ولا تنحرفوا عما حد لكم بإفراط وتفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition parallels another sūra's command not to follow unbelievers' desires: avoiding them preserves full steadfastness, while following them is transgression.
rows.anchor: والنهيان متقاربان إذ المراد عدم الاتباع لإهواء أهل الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading assigns the afternoon edge of day to noon and afternoon prayers, and the night approaches to sunset and night prayers, covering all five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: الظهر والعصر لأن ما بعد الزوال عشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes the day's ends as morning and sunset and night approaches as night prayer plus tahajjud, obligatory for the Prophet; it cites the night vigil command.
rows.anchor: وفسر بعضهم طرفي النهار بالصبح والمغرب وزلف الليل بالعشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations include witr according to Abū Ḥanīfa, or night prayer, witr, and tahajjud together, matching the plural ‘approaches.’
rows.anchor: أو الوتر على ما ذهب إليه أبو حنيفة أو مجموع العشاء والوتر والتهجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A similar passage is read as morning before sunrise, noon and afternoon before sunset, and sunset and night prayers at night.
rows.anchor: أي : بصلاة الصبح [ق : 39-79]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good deeds, especially the five prayers, erase consequences of minor sins rather than undoing sins already committed; prayers, Fridays, and Ramadans expiate between them when major sins are avoided.
rows.anchor: على الإطلاق لا سيما الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer also restrains people from committing sins, as another verse says it keeps one from indecency and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: إن الصلوة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر

rows.speaker: أبو اليسر الأنصاري
rows.claim: Abū al-Yusr was tempted by a woman buying dates; he drew her home, embraced and kissed her but stopped before intercourse when she warned him to fear God, then regretted it.
rows.anchor: أن أبا اليسر الأنصاري كان يبيع التمر فأتته امرأة

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū al-Yusr confessed to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, who advised concealing the sin and repenting, but he could not keep silent and went to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فأتى أبا بكر رضي الله عنه فأخبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet told him to wait for God's command; after the afternoon prayer the verse came, and prayer expiated his act for everyone.
rows.anchor: فلما صلى صلاة العصر نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet compares five daily prayers to bathing five times in a river at one's door, which leaves no dirt behind.
rows.anchor: لو أن نهرا بباب أحدكم يغتسل منه كل يوم خمس مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sins are impurities and acts of obedience purify; ablution washes away sins with its drops, so some jurists considered used ablution cloth impure and disliked praying in it.
rows.anchor: أن الذنوب كلها نجاسات والطاعات مطهرات وبماء أعضاء الوضوء تتساقط الأوزار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report has God tell Moses that each drop of ablution water used by Aḥmad and his community earns a garden as broad as the sky.
rows.anchor: يتوضأ أحمد وأمته كما أمرتهم وأعطيهم بكل قطرة

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Ḥāfiẓ's Persian couplet praises prayer and devoted appeal purified by tears and heart's blood.
rows.anchor: خوشا نماز ونياز كسى كه ازسردرد بآب ديده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest good deed is knowledge of God, following monotheism, and opposing the lower self; remembrance purifies souls and hearts, strengthens obedience, and defeats Satan's schemes.
rows.anchor: العلم بالله ، وطريقه التوحيد ، وخلاف هوى النفس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When companions ask whether ‘There is no god but God’ is a good deed, the Prophet says it is the best of good deeds.
rows.anchor: لا إله إلا الله من الحسنات قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse signals constant remembrance, worship, and obedience by day and night, with time for human needs, daytime work, and sleep to restore tired faculties for worship.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى إدامة الذكر والطاعة والعبادة في الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, light from good deeds, remembrance, and watchfulness at day edges and night approaches erases the darkness of time spent on bodily needs.
rows.anchor: أي أن أنوار الحسنات وهي الأعمال الصالحة والذكر والمراقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The luminous spirit would be lost through attachment to the dark body unless sacred good works nurture it, lift it toward spirituality and divine unity, and dispel bodily darkness.
rows.anchor: تعلق الروح النوراني العلوي بالجسد الظلماني السفلي موجب لخسران الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares this nurture to a seed that would be lost unless water made one seed into seven hundred, with God multiplying further as He wills.
rows.anchor: كما أن إلقاء الحبة في الأرض موجب لخسران الحبة
